bug_info.bug_desc: In the pre-fix pwrmgr, `esc_timeout` is a non-persistent timeout indication generated by `u_esc_timeout`. It is used directly as the escalation reset request (`peri_reqs_raw.rstreqs[ResetEscIdx]`) and as the write-enable for `fault_status.esc_timeout`. When the escalation clock restarts after a long stoppage, `esc_timeout` can deassert before the reset request or fault status has been captured, so the escalation timeout condition is lost and no escalation reset is generated. The timeout condition must be held until reset, similar to `esc_rst_req_q`.
bug_info.fix_hint: Synchronize `esc_timeout` into the `clk_lc`/`rst_lc_n` domain with a 2-flop synchronizer, then latch it in a sticky flop (`esc_timeout_lc_q`) that is set when the timeout is detected and cleared only by `rst_lc_n`. Use this latched `esc_timeout_lc_q` instead of the raw `esc_timeout` both in the OR that forms `peri_reqs_raw.rstreqs[ResetEscIdx]` and in `hw2reg.fault_status.esc_timeout.de`. Apply the same change consistently to both the template and autogen copies of `pwrmgr.sv`.
